minutes.headline: Committee set 4% yearly preschool tuition increases for three years and kept 9th-grade school choice closed.
minutes.summary: The superintendent announced her retirement at the end of the school year. The committee declined to open ninth-grade school choice but allowed it for students already enrolled in grades 10-12. Most of the meeting went to preschool tuition and the space and teacher needs behind it. It also waived the first reading of a naming and memorials policy, approved the 2018-2019 calendar, and heard a brief budget outlook before going into executive session.

what_happened.line: The committee voted to raise the preschool daily rate 4 percent a year for fiscal years 2019, 2020 and 2021 at the Early Learning Center.
The committee voted not to open any ninth-grade school choice slots for 2018-19, then allowed choice for current students moving into grades 10-12.
The superintendent announced her retirement at the end of the school year.
The committee waived the full first reading of the naming and memorials policy; it returns at the next meeting and will be posted for public feedback.
The committee accepted the revised 2018-2019 school calendar, and the superintendent said the governor's budget was a disappointment on Chapter 70 and that she is seeking circuit breaker relief.

why_it_matters: Preschool families face a set 4 percent yearly tuition rise through fiscal 2021, while the minutes record that tuition covers only a small share of the program's teacher and aide salaries.
Closing ninth-grade school choice keeps the incoming class from growing by choice students, and Chapter 70 aid in the governor's budget bears on the town budget, mostly taxes, in the coming year.
watch_next: The naming and memorials policy returns at the next School Committee meeting and will be posted for public feedback.
The superintendent is seeking circuit breaker relief, and the state budget's Chapter 70 figure for the district remains to be set.
